raw_response:
I am old now, 71, and only have 2 mu, so I do not do fancy things. I farm the same wheat-maize rotation I have done for many years because it feeds us and gives some cash. On such a small piece of land, I cannot afford to gamble. If the year looks normal, I will plant wheat after the autumn maize comes off, and after the wheat harvest in June, I will put maize in right away. I watch what the neighbors do and I follow what has worked on my own land. If I see the crop looking weak, I add a bit more, but I do not change too much.

For wheat, I will use the local seed I can easily buy, not expensive special seed. Before sowing, I will spread farmyard manure if I have some and put a base fertilizer in the field, then after winter if the wheat looks yellow, I will topdress urea once around jointing. Wheat is important, so I would rather not let it go hungry. I have a well, so I will probably water about three times if rain is normal: once before winter or at overwintering if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once around grain filling if needed. For maize, the time is tight after wheat harvest, so I will not do heavy tillage. I usually clear the wheat, turn the soil lightly or just make rows, and plant quickly. Maize on my land does not need as much water as wheat, but if summer rain is poor, I will water once or twice. I do not spray unless I see a real problem. Money is tight, so every extra bag of fertilizer or every irrigation means less cash left in hand, but cutting too much is also risky because then yield falls.
